newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rubber stable in late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rubber stable in late trading.

text.p: Indonesian tyre-grade SIR20 rubber prices were generally stable in late trading amid thin buying interest, traders said.
"There has been some interest albeit thin. But buyers seem to want to wait a bit before making decisions. Maybe, they want to wait until prices ease," said one trader in Palembang, south Sumatra.
Traders said they were waiting for the International Natural Rubber Organisation (INRO) to enter the market, adding that prices were close to the grouping's "may buy" level.
"We are monitoring INRO because we heard it had started to circulate forms to U.S. dealers outling terms and conditions under which they can buy rubber from INRO," one trader said.
Traders offer prices were stable at 43.50 U.S. cents/lb for September shipment fob Medan and at 43.25 fob Palembang. Offers were quoted at 43.00 fob Padang, Surabaya, Pontianak and Jambi.

Traders said the INRO five-day moving average price was currently close to the group's "may-buy" level of 183.00 Malaysian/Singapore cents. INRO's "must-buy" level -- when the grouping must intervene in the market by purchasing rubber to pull up prices -- is 10 cents below the "may-buy" level.
